headline: UPDATE to totw-20261029-0300-05 (Israel election) -- Petek count advances 97.63% -> 98.01% at 01
dek: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] The Petek tracker now shows 98.01% of ballots counted at 01:28 (5,123,252 valid votes, 11,757 polling stations, 1,203 localities), up from 97.63% (5,102,165 valid votes, 11,712 stations) at the 03:00 scan's standing figure. Seat projection is UNCHANGED: Netanyahu bloc 53,…
sources: The Petek live tracker (CEC-sourced per tracker)
fault_line: Who forms the government -- and do the 19 Arab-party seats kingmake, back a minority government from outside, or stay out while both blocs stay short of 61?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] The Petek tracker now shows 98.01% of ballots counted at 01:28 (5,123,252 valid votes, 11,757 polling stations, 1,203 localities), up from 97.63% (5,102,165 valid votes, 11,712 stations) at the 03:00 scan's standing figure. Seat projection is UNCHANGED: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot-led Change bloc 48, Arab parties 19, nobody at 61. The tracker display does not distinguish whether the +21,087-vote increment is double-envelope ballots (count began 03:00 ) or late ordinary ballots -- do not claim either. Double-envelope count expected complete Thursday evening; official results Nov 4.
sections.what_verified: Petek tracker (CEC-sourced per tracker; no declared tier in the registry) for the new figure; the frozen 53-48-19 split is consistent across Times of Israel (T3), i24 and Indian Express reporting of the same count stage. Single family for the NEW figure itself.
sections.what_disputed: Haaretz's 89.8% figure still circulating in search results is OLDER than 98.01% and must not be re-reported as new. Likud's fraud allegation against Arab parties (recorded Oct 28) is unproven; the CEC says every inquiry will be examined.
sections.why_matters: Proven-set follow-up: the count moves but the deadlock does not -- lead with the frozen 53-48-19 against 98.01% counted, not with the increment. The story is the arithmetic, not the turnout.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261029-0300-05 (Israel election) -- Petek count advances 97.63% -> 98.01% at 01:28 Oct 29 (tracker local time = 03:28 on the tracker's Israel-time convention, in-window); seats FROZEN at 53-48-19; valid votes 5,123,252 (+21,087)

totw_analysis: Our read: Proven-set follow-up: the count moves but the deadlock does not -- lead with the frozen 53-48-19 against 98.01% counted, not with the increment. The story is the arithmetic, not the turnout. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who forms the government -- and do the 19 Arab-party seats kingmake, back a minority government from outside, or stay out while both blocs stay short of 61?
